explain.say: In 1968 Fairchild released the 741, a whole amplifier on one chip, and op-amps have been in mixers, sensors and instruments ever since. On the board, a 0.5 volt input feeds a 10 kilohm resistor into the op-amp's minus input, and a 100 kilohm feedback resistor runs from the output back to that same input. The plus input is grounded.

parts.label: Op-amp
parts.ask: What are the golden rules of op-amps?

explain.say: An op-amp is an amplifier with enormous gain, a hundred thousand or more. Wrap negative feedback round it and two golden rules appear. One: no current flows into its inputs. Two: the output does whatever it takes to make the two inputs equal. The plus input is grounded, so the minus input sits at 0 volts too, a virtual earth. Is it actually wired to ground?

draw.text: With negative feedback: no input current, and V+ = V−.

explain.say: No, the feedback holds it there. Now follow the current. The input resistor has 0.5 volts across it, so 50 microamps flow through 10 kilohms. That current can't enter the op-amp, so all of it continues through the feedback resistor. 50 microamps through 100 kilohms drops 5 volts, and with one end at 0 volts the output must be minus 5 volts. Why minus?

parts.label: R_f (feedback)
parts.ask: Why is the output of an inverting amplifier negative?

parts.label: Op-amp
parts.ask: What are the golden rules of op-amps?

explain.say: The current flows from the virtual earth towards the output, so the output sits below zero. The gain is minus R f over R in, minus 10, set only by two resistors, not by the op-amp's wild internal gain. On the plot, the output is ten times bigger and upside down. What would the gain be with a 47 kilohm feedback resistor?

curves.label: Output, gain −10
curves.ask: Why is the output of an inverting amplifier negative?

explain.say: Minus 4.7. Superb! Add more input resistors to the virtual earth and their currents simply add: that is the summing amplifier at the heart of an audio mixer. One limit: the output can't go beyond the supply. On plus and minus 12 volts, a 1.5 volt input asks for minus 15 and clips near minus 12. Challenge: choose R f for a gain of minus 20 with a 4.7 kilohm input resistor.

faq.a: An op-amp circuit where the input goes through R in to the minus input and R f feeds back from the output. Its gain is minus R f over R in.
asks: How does an inverting op amp work?

faq.a: With the plus input grounded and negative feedback, the op-amp holds its minus input at almost exactly 0 volts, even though it is not wired to ground.

faq.q: What are the golden rules of op-amps?
faq.a: With negative feedback: no current flows into either input, and the output does whatever it takes to make the two input voltages equal.

faq.q: Why is the output of an inverting amplifier negative?
faq.a: The input current flows through R f away from the virtual earth towards the output, so for a positive input the output must sit below 0 volts.
asks: Why does an inverting amplifier invert?

faq.a: The output cannot go beyond its supply rails, and usually stops a volt or so short of them. Asking for more causes clipping.

facts: Fairchild Semiconductor introduced the µA741 op-amp in 1968.
Real op-amps have open-loop gains of around 100,000 or more, which is why feedback resistors alone set the closed-loop gain.

quiz.say: An inverting amplifier has an input resistor of 2 kilohms, a feedback resistor of 20 kilohms, and an input of 0.3 volts. What is the output?
quiz.show: R_in = 2 kΩ, R_f = 20 kΩ and the input is 0.3 V. What is the output of the inverting amplifier?
quiz.why: The gain is minus 20 over 2, minus 10, so 0.3 volts becomes minus 3 volts.

wrong.1: An inverting amplifier flips the sign.
wrong.2: That divides by 10 instead of multiplying.

quiz.say: In an inverting amplifier with its plus input grounded, what voltage does the minus input sit at?
quiz.show: In an inverting amplifier with its + input grounded, the − input sits at...
quiz.why: Negative feedback makes the two inputs equal, and the plus input is at 0 volts: a virtual earth.

wrong.1: The input voltage is across R in, not at the minus pin.
wrong.2: The minus pin stays near zero while the output does the work.
